items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: so they happened to be the owner of the Birdland, so as soon that they opened we played maybe twenty times. ... He sent a letter of permission to make those two albums.

ctx.x: Did anybody suggest that these musicians record with the Machito orchestra?; because the Roost label belonged to Morris Levy, to Teddy Reig, to Jack Cook and Symphony Sid. They were four partners in that label and in Bop City and the Royal Roost. Did any of them suggest Howard Mcghee and Brew Moore? Brew Moore is a white Jewish musician, Howard McGhee is an Afro-American, they fitted-in so well on that recording that they have a lot of Afro-Cuban in them. Wouldn't you say?

Well, you name me four guys that was involved with jazz all their lives. The young one was Morris Levy, very talented, a good promoter, a good - he had idea of what-- He had a good idea of marketing as good as Symphony Sid and the other guy and the other guy, because - and what you call it, the first fellow, ahhh ....
